title: The token as the unit
subtitle: Schedule, budget and account for GPU work in the unit the hardware actually pays in

stats.label: padding waste across two NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs
cache hit rate on the same pair
tokens received, balanced against the same number routed

lede: Queues move messages. Schedulers count jobs. Budgets count dollars or requests. None of those is what a GPU pays in. A GPU pays in tokens, and its cost for a batch depends on the shape of those tokens: how long each sequence is, how much of each prefix is shared with its neighbours, how much padding the batch carries, whether the cache already holds the work. Once I made the token the unit of scheduling, packing, budgeting and accounting, a whole class of inefficiency became visible and fixable. Work is described to the scheduler by its token geometry. Batches are packed to a consumer's declared token limits, not to a count of items.
quote: The broker must not know the model; it must know only what the consumer needs to pack well, and four integers turn out to be enough.
evidence: Token-aware scheduling: shape-pure batches packed to each consumer's declared token limits, with 0.42% padding waste and a 99.9% cache hit rate across two NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs.
Distributed systems correctness: token accounting that balanced 12.3 B tokens received against the same number routed.
author: Corey James
